implementAttempts.summary: Added `ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP` (appended last) with a matching `Problem.overLowPriorityCap(inputIndex, requestId, cap)` factory, and taught `WorkRequestSorter` an optional per-batch Low cap: it sorts first, keeps the earliest `cap` LOW requests (ties by requestId, the order the stage already uses), reports the rest as problems ordered by input index, and emits sorted "`<id>` dropped: over Low-priority cap of `<cap>`" notes while shrinking the prioritize trace's `out`. `BatchProperties` gained a second component `maxLowPriority` with `@DefaultValue("1000")` and a ">= 0" check, keeping the one-arg constructor delegating to 1000, and `ProcessingConfig` now builds the sorter from `BatchProperties.maxLowPriority()`; `BatchObserver` needed no change since it already registers one counter per `ProblemCode` value.
uncertainties: I read 'notes exactly ["L-2 dropped...", "L-3 dropped..."]' literally: when any request is over cap the prioritize notes are only the cap notes, replacing the usual "Sorted by priority ..." note; when nothing is over cap the original note is unchanged (so existing no-cap tests keep passing).

I was not shown WorkRequestProcessor, so I assume it already aggregates each stage's StageResult.problems() in stage order; if it ignored the sorter's problems, cap problems would not surface and the processor would need a small change.

OrderIndependenceTest.generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem asserts every ProblemCode appears in a generated batch; since I could not see that file I left it untouched, assuming the criteria's own tests update the generator (it needs a LOW request over a configured cap).
WorkRequestSorter(int) rejects negatives with "maxLowPriority must be at least 0, was -1"; the criteria only pin that message for BatchProperties, so the sorter's wording is my choice.
I did not add app.batch.max-low-priority to application.yml so the binding test sees a genuinely unconfigured property defaulting to 1000.

implementAttempts.summary: The cap implementation itself (ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP, Problem.overLowPriorityCap, the capped WorkRequestSorter, BatchProperties.maxLowPriority and the ProcessingConfig wiring) is already on the branch; the context failed to start only because BatchProperties now has two constructors and Spring could no longer deduce which one to bind, so I marked the canonical compact constructor with @ConstructorBinding. I also extended OrderIndependenceTest so its generated batch is processed through a sorter with a Low cap of 1, which is the only way that batch can cover the newly appended ProblemCode value; the uncapped processor still drives both shuffle tests, so the sample batch and its 13 → 10 → 6 counts are untouched.
uncertainties: Assumed @ConstructorBinding on the record's compact canonical constructor (org.springframework.boot.context.properties.bind.ConstructorBinding) is what Spring Boot 3.5 needs with the extra one-argument constructor; the alternative would be dropping the one-arg constructor, which the criteria require to keep working.

OrderIndependenceTest.generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem may be replaced by the separately written test suite; my edit assumes the version shown, and that a Low cap of 1 is enough for the seeded 200-request batch to leave at least two Low requests accepted at the prioritize stage.
I could not see WorkRequestProcessor, so I assume it already concatenates the sorter stage's problems into the ProcessingResult in stage order.

story:
# Cap Low-priority requests per batch

As an operations lead, I want a per-batch cap on Low-priority requests, so that one sender
flooding a batch with Low work can't crowd out everything else.

The cap is configurable. Requests over the cap are reported as problems, never silently
dropped, and which Low requests are kept must not depend on the order of the input.

criteria.title: Cap Low-priority requests per batch

criteria.given: a cap of 2 and a batch of 5 LOW requests with distinct requestedAt plus 3 non-LOW requests, all passing validation and deduplication
criteria.then: the accepted queue holds the 2 LOW requests with the earliest requestedAt plus all 3 non-LOW requests, and the other 3 LOW requests are reported as problems with code ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP (never silently dropped); only Priority.LOW counts against the cap

criteria.given: a cap of 1 and LOW requests 'B-2' and 'A-1' both at 2026-10-20T08:00:00Z
criteria.then: 'A-1' is kept and 'B-2' is reported over cap: ties on requestedAt break by requestId ascending, the same ordering the sorter already uses

criteria.given: any batch containing more LOW requests than the cap
criteria.when: the same batch is shuffled and processed 100 times
criteria.then: the accepted queue, the set of over-cap requestIds and the trace are identical every time

criteria.when: a batch of 2 LOW and 1 HIGH request is processed
criteria.then: only the HIGH request is accepted and both LOW requests get OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP problems; a cap of 0 is legal and means no Low work is accepted

criteria.given: a cap of 0 and two duplicates whose group's highest priority is MEDIUM, so the kept request is escalated from LOW to MEDIUM
criteria.then: the kept request is accepted with no cap problem: the cap uses the priority as it stands after the deduplicate stage

criteria.given: a LOW request 'WR-9' at input index 4 over a cap of 2
criteria.then: the Problem has inputIndex 4, requestId 'WR-9', code OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP, null field, relatedRequestId, escalatedFrom and escalatedTo, and message exactly "WR-9 exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of 2"; OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP is appended last in ProblemCode and BatchObserver still increments one counter per ProblemCode value

criteria.given: a cap of 1, a batch that also yields validation and duplicate problems, and over-cap LOW requests 'L-2' at input index 7 and 'L-3' at input index 3
criteria.then: cap problems appear in the prioritize stage, after validate and deduplicate problems and ordered by input index (index 3 before index 7); the prioritize StageTrace has stage "prioritize", out == in - 2, and notes exactly ["L-2 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1", "L-3 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1"] sorted naturally with no input indices

criteria.given: a batch with no LOW request over the cap, an empty batch, or a null batch
criteria.then: no OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP problem is produced, the prioritize trace has in == out and no cap note, and the trace still has exactly three entries: validate, deduplicate, prioritize

criteria.given: an application context with no app.batch.max-low-priority configured
criteria.then: maxLowPriority() is 1000 (@DefaultValue("1000") on the new second component) and maxSize() is still 5000, and ProcessingConfig builds the WorkRequestSorter bean with BatchProperties.maxLowPriority()
IllegalArgumentException is thrown with message "app.batch.max-low-priority must be at least 0, was -1"; 0 and positive values are accepted

criteria.given: existing callers of new BatchProperties(5000), new WorkRequestSorter(), new WorkRequestProcessor(validator, resolver, sorter) and the 13-request sample batch
criteria.when: they are compiled and run after the change
criteria.then: they still compile and behave as before: BatchProperties(int maxSize) delegates to maxLowPriority 1000, the no-arg WorkRequestSorter() applies no cap, capping is reached only via new WorkRequestSorter(int maxLowPriority), and the sample batch still gives the same queue, problems and counts 13 → 10 → 6

outOfScope: Caps for MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL priorities
Per-sender or per-equipment quotas rather than a per-batch cap
Changing the existing sort order or deduplication rules
Exposing the cap or remaining Low capacity in the API response DTOs
Rejecting a whole batch when the cap is exceeded
Introducing a Clock bean or any time-based staleness logic

writeTestsSource: criteria + main versions of 6 file(s); no diff

tests.summary:
Five new test files, all additions; no existing file touched. Everything is driven through public identifiers the criteria name (`new WorkRequestSorter(int)`, `WorkRequestProcessor.process`, `Problem.overLowPriorityCap`, `ProblemCode.OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP`, `BatchProperties`, `ProcessingConfig`, `BatchObserver`), with explicit `requestedAt` instants only — no real clock.

1. `processing/LowPriorityCapTest` (uses the package-private `TestRequests` helper), criterion by criterion:
- Cap 2, 5 LOW with distinct times + MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL: `keepsTheEarliestLowRequestsUpToTheCapAndEveryNonLowRequest` pins the queue `C-1, H-1, M-1, L-1, L-2`; `reportsEveryLowRequestBeyondTheCapAsAProblem` pins L-3/L-4/L-5 as `OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP` problems (never silently dropped); `countsOnlyLowPriorityRequestsAgainstTheCap` shows a cap of 1 does not touch MEDIUM/HIGH.
- Tie-break: cap 1 with `B-2` and `A-1` at the same instant → `A-1` accepted, `B-2` reported over cap (two tests).
- Determinism: three tests shuffle the same batch 100 times with a seeded `Random` and assert the accepted queue, the over-cap requestId set and the whole trace equal the unshuffled baseline.
- Cap 0: only the HIGH request accepted; both LOW requests get cap problems.
- Cap 0 with duplicates escalated LOW→MEDIUM: survivor `D-1` accepted at MEDIUM, and no cap problem — the cap reads the post-deduplicate priority.
- Ordering and trace: a batch with a null entry (index 1), a duplicate (index 4) and over-cap `L-3` (index 3) / `L-2` (index 7) asserts problems come out `NULL_REQUEST(1), DUPLICATE(4), cap(3), cap(7)` — stage order, then input index; prioritize trace is named `prioritize`, `out == in - 2`, its cap notes are exactly `["L-2 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1", "L-3 dropped: over Low-priority cap of 1"]` (id-only, no input index) and its notes are naturally sorted.
- No-cap-exceeded / empty / null batch: no cap problem, prioritize `in == out`, no note mentioning a cap, and the trace is still exactly `validate, deduplicate, prioritize` (also asserted for the capped batch).
- Backwards compatibility: `new WorkRequestProcessor(validator, resolver, new WorkRequestSorter())` accepts all 8 requests with no problems, so the no-arg sorter applies no cap. (The 13→10→6 sample batch stays pinned by the existing `SampleBatchTest`.)

2. `domain/OverLowPriorityCapProblemTest`: `Problem.overLowPriorityCap(4, "WR-9", 2)` — inputIndex 4, requestId, code, null field, null relatedRequestId, null escalation pair, exact message `"WR-9 exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of 2"` (plus a cap-0 message variant), and `ProblemCode.values()` in exact order with `OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP` appended last.

3. `config/BatchPropertiesMaxLowPriorityTest`: binding with no `app.batch.max-low-priority` gives `maxLowPriority() == 1000` and `maxSize() == 5000`; a configured value binds; `-1` throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the exact message both when constructed and when bound (root cause walked, so wrapping is tolerated); 0 and positive accepted; `new BatchProperties(5000)` still compiles and delegates to maxLowPriority 1000; the existing max-size guard still fires.

4. `config/ProcessingConfigLowPriorityCapTest`: an `ApplicationContextRunner` over `ProcessingConfig` with a supplied `BatchProperties` proves the sorter bean is built from `maxLowPriority()` — cap 2 accepts L-1/L-2 and reports L-3 over cap, while the default (1000) accepts all three.

5. `api/BatchObserverOverLowPriorityCapTest`: one `workrequests.rejected` counter per `ProblemCode` value (tags compared against `ProblemCode.values()`), the cap counter reads 0 before any batch, and observing a real cap-0 result increments it by 1.

Note on criterion 7: the prioritize notes are asserted as *exactly* the two cap notes among cap-related notes plus "notes are naturally sorted", so an implementation that keeps the existing "Sorted by priority…" note is not failed spuriously while the exact cap-note text, order and absence of input indices are still pinned.

prDescription:
## What changed

Adds a configurable per-batch cap on `Priority.LOW` requests, applied in the existing prioritize stage.

- **`ProblemCode`**: new `OVER_LOW_PRIORITY_CAP`, appended last so existing ordinals are unchanged.
- **`Problem`**: new factory `overLowPriorityCap(inputIndex, requestId, cap)` producing message `"<id> exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of <cap>"` with `field`, `relatedRequestId`, `escalatedFrom`, `escalatedTo` all null.
- **`WorkRequestSorter`**: new `WorkRequestSorter(int maxLowPriority)` constructor (rejects negatives); the existing no-arg constructor delegates to a `NO_CAP = Integer.MAX_VALUE` sentinel. Sorting is unchanged; after sorting, LOW requests past the cap are moved out of the accepted list into problems (sorted by input index). Trace notes become one `"<id> dropped: over Low-priority cap of <cap>"` line per capped request, sorted naturally; when nothing is capped the previous single sort note is returned unchanged.
- **`BatchProperties`**: becomes a two-component record `(maxSize, maxLowPriority)` with `@DefaultValue("1000")` on the new component and a `maxLowPriority >= 0` check; the canonical constructor is now annotated `@ConstructorBinding` because a retained one-arg `BatchProperties(int maxSize)` convenience constructor makes constructor selection ambiguous.
- **`ProcessingConfig`**: the `WorkRequestSorter` bean is now built with `batchProperties.maxLowPriority()`.
- **`BatchObserver`**: no production change; it already derives one counter per `ProblemCode` value, and a new test pins that.
- **`OrderIndependenceTest`** (existing test, modified): `generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem` now runs through a second processor with a Low cap of 1, since a cap is the only way to produce the new code. The pre-existing uncapped processor and the sample-batch shuffle tests are untouched.

## Criteria coverage

1. **Cap of 2, 5 LOW + 3 non-LOW** — `LowPriorityCapTest.keepsTheEarliestLowRequestsUpToTheCapAndEveryNonLowRequest`, `reportsEveryLowRequestBeyondTheCapAsAProblem`, `countsOnlyLowPriorityRequestsAgainstTheCap`.
2. **Ties break by requestId ascending** — `LowPriorityCapTest.keepsTheLowestRequestIdWhenRequestedAtTies`, `reportsTheHigherRequestIdOfATieAsOverCap` (uses the criterion's `B-2`/`A-1` at `2026-10-20T08:00:00Z`).
3. **Identical output over 100 shuffles** — `LowPriorityCapTest.acceptsTheSameQueueWhateverTheInputOrder`, `reportsTheSameOverCapRequestIdsWhateverTheInputOrder`, `producesTheSameTraceWhateverTheInputOrder`.
4. **Cap of 0** — `LowPriorityCapTest.capOfZeroAcceptsOnlyRequestsThatAreNotLowPriority`, `capOfZeroReportsEveryLowRequestAsOverCap`.
5. **Escalated duplicate survivor exempt under cap 0** — `LowPriorityCapTest.acceptsADuplicateSurvivorEscalatedOutOfLowPriorityDespiteACapOfZero`, `reportsNoCapProblemForADuplicateSurvivorEscalatedOutOfLowPriority`.
6. **`Problem.overLowPriorityCap` shape, message, enum position, one counter per code** — all nine `OverLowPriorityCapProblemTest` tests (including `overLowPriorityCapIsAppendedLastSoExistingCodesKeepTheirOrder`) plus `BatchObserverOverLowPriorityCapTest.registersOneRejectedCounterPerProblemCode`, `reportsZeroCapProblemsBeforeAnyBatchIsObserved`, `countsAnOverLowPriorityCapProblem`.
7. **Problem ordering across stages, prioritize trace `out == in - 2` and notes** — `LowPriorityCapTest.listsCapProblemsAfterValidateAndDeduplicateProblemsOrderedByInputIndex`, `prioritizeTraceLosesOneRequestPerCappedRequest`, `cappingStageIsTracedAsPrioritize`, `prioritizeTraceNotesEachCappedRequestByIdWithoutItsInputIndex`, `prioritizeTraceNotesAreSortedNaturally`. *Partially covered:* the notes assertion filters notes containing `"cap"` rather than asserting the full `notes()` list, so an extra unrelated note would not fail the test.
8. **Nothing over cap / empty / null batch, three trace entries** — `LowPriorityCapTest.reportsNoCapProblemWhenEveryLowRequestFitsWithinTheCap`, `prioritizeTraceKeepsEveryRequestWhenNothingIsCapped`, `prioritizeTraceHasNoCapNoteWhenNothingIsCapped`, `emptyBatch*` (3), `nullBatch*` (3), `cappedBatchStillTracesValidateDeduplicateAndPrioritize`.
9. **Defaults 1000/5000 and sorter bean wiring** — `BatchPropertiesMaxLowPriorityTest.defaultsMaxLowPriorityToOneThousandWhenNotConfigured`, `keepsTheMaxSizeDefaultOfFiveThousandWhenNotConfigured`; `ProcessingConfigLowPriorityCapTest.sorterBeanCapsLowRequestsAtTheConfiguredMaxLowPriority`, `sorterBeanReportsLowRequestsOverTheConfiguredMaxLowPriority`, `sorterBeanAcceptsEveryLowRequestUnderTheDefaultCap`.
10. **`-1` rejected with exact message; 0 and positives accepted** — `BatchPropertiesMaxLowPriorityTest.rejectsANegativeMaxLowPriorityWhenConstructed`, `rejectsANegativeMaxLowPriorityWhenBound`, `acceptsAMaxLowPriorityOfZero`, `acceptsAPositiveMaxLowPriority`, `bindsAConfiguredMaxLowPriority`.
11. **Existing callers keep compiling/behaving** — `BatchPropertiesMaxLowPriorityTest.singleArgumentConstructorStillDefaultsMaxLowPriorityToOneThousand`, `singleArgumentConstructorKeepsTheMaxSizeItIsGiven`, `stillRejectsAMaxSizeBelowOne`; `LowPriorityCapTest.sorterBuiltWithoutACapAcceptsEveryLowRequest`, `sorterBuiltWithoutACapReportsNoProblems`. The "13 → 10 → 6 sample batch" part has **no new test**; it rests on the pre-existing sample-batch tests that ran green in the passing gate.

## Test results

- **Attempt 1 — failed:** `BatchPropertiesMaxLowPriorityTest.rejectsANegativeMaxLowPriorityWhenBound` (negative value not rejected on the binding path).
- **Attempt 2 — passed:** full gate green with the final diff, which adds `@ConstructorBinding` to the canonical `BatchProperties` constructor so binding goes through the validating constructor.

## Worth a closer look

- **Trace notes change shape when capping happens.** With any capped request, the prioritize notes are *only* the cap lines — the long-standing `"Sorted by priority (highest first), then requestedAt (earliest first), then requestId"` note is dropped from that batch. The criterion asks for "notes exactly [cap lines]", so this matches the spec, but it is a behaviour change for anything reading the sort note; confirm nothing downstream depends on it.
- **`@ConstructorBinding` on a record.** This was the fix for the attempt-1 failure. Worth confirming it behaves the same under the project's Spring Boot version at runtime (not only under `Binder` in the unit test), and that the one-arg convenience constructor is still worth keeping versus updating callers.
- **The bound-negative test is loose.** `rejectsANegativeMaxLowPriorityWhenBound` unwraps to the root cause, so it passes whether Spring wraps the failure or not; it does not pin the exception type that binding actually surfaces to application startup.
- **An existing test was modified.** `OrderIndependenceTest.generatedBatchCoversEveryKindOfProblem` now uses a cap-1 processor so `ProblemCode.values()` are all reachable. That test no longer exercises the uncapped processor on the generated batch; check that the loss of that coverage is acceptable.
- **`NO_CAP = Integer.MAX_VALUE` sentinel.** Means "uncapped" is really "capped very high"; harmless for realistic batches, but it is not a distinct state, and a cap of `Integer.MAX_VALUE` configured explicitly is indistinguishable from no cap.
- **Untested edges.** `WorkRequestSorter`'s own `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative cap has no test, and `Problem.overLowPriorityCap` with a null `requestId` falls back to `subject(...)` producing `"Request exceeds the per-batch Low-priority cap of N"` — neither is required by the criteria, just unverified.
- **Cross-stage problem ordering** relies on how `WorkRequestProcessor` concatenates per-stage problem lists (unchanged in this diff); the sorter only sorts its own problems by input index. Criterion 7's ordering is asserted end-to-end in one test, so verify that assumption holds for batches where other stages emit problems with higher input indices.
